title: The rest that remains and the priest who sympathizes

passage.why: Chapter 3 ended with a generation that could not enter God's rest. Chapter 4 opens the door again, then introduces Jesus as the great high priest who understands us from the inside.

readAloud: Since then we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession. For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tempted as we are, yet without sin. Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need. (Hebrews 4:14-16)
setting: The author keeps reading Psalm 95. If Joshua had given Israel final rest in Canaan, God would not have spoken centuries later through David of 'another day' (4:7-8). So the land was a picture. The rest is God's own seventh-day rest (Genesis 2:2), still open 'today' to all who believe.

sections.heading: A Sabbath rest remains
sections.body: 'So then, there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God, for whoever has entered God's rest has also rested from his works as God did from his' (4:9-10). It is entered by faith ('we who have believed enter that rest', 4:3) and yet we are to 'strive to enter that rest' (4:11). Rest is received, and it takes effort to keep receiving it.

sections.heading: The word that sees us
sections.body: 'The word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword... discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart' (4:12). The same word that offers rest also exposes the hard heart. 'All are naked and exposed to the eyes of him to whom we must give account' (4:13). Then, at once, the high priest.

sections.heading: The great high priest
sections.body: Jesus was 'in every respect... tempted as we are, yet without sin' (4:15). Every high priest is chosen from among men to deal gently with the ignorant and wayward (5:1-2). Jesus did not appoint himself; God did (Psalm 2:7 and 110:4 in 5:5-6). In Gethsemane he 'offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears' (5:7), and 'learned obedience through what he suffered' (5:8).

sections.heading: How does the Sabbath apply now?
sections.body: Christians differ: Saturday rest kept as a command, Sunday as the Christian Sabbath, or a Sabbath principle without a fixed day, fulfilled in Christ (Romans 14:5-6; Colossians 2:16-17). Hebrews 4 agrees that the deepest rest is in Christ. Your family's Saturday conviction stands; this is worth an hour with your pastor.

observe: How many times does 'rest' appear in 4:1-11? What is it each time: Canaan, God's seventh day, or something still ahead?
Compare 4:12-13 with 4:14-16. Why might the author put exposure and mercy side by side?
List what Jesus shares with every high priest (5:1-4) and what is unique to him (5:5-10).

words.note: A rare word, perhaps coined here: a Sabbath-keeping or Sabbath celebration. Not just a stop, but a feast of rest (4:9).
To suffer with, to feel with. Jesus does not observe our weakness from outside (4:15).
Boldness, freedom of speech: the right to speak openly before the throne (4:16; 10:19).

crossRefs.note: God rested on the seventh day: the rest Hebrews points to.
Canaan's rest was real but not final.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
Gethsemane: the loud cries and tears of Hebrews 5:7.
The Psalm the whole section preaches.

reflect: Where am I striving to earn rest rather than striving to enter it?
What weakness do I hide from God that Hebrews 4:15 says Jesus already understands?
What would it look like this week to draw near 'with confidence' instead of with shame?

practice.name: A Sabbath of receiving
practice.how: Today, before any task, read 4:9-10 and 4:14-16 aloud. Name one work you are resting from and one weakness you are bringing to the throne of grace. Then do one thing purely for delight with your family.

pray: Adoration: the high priest who passed through the heavens. Confession: the weaknesses I hide. Thanksgiving: mercy and grace to help in time of need. Supplication: for rest, at home and at Eden.
journalPrompts: What did I learn about God this week, from the reading or from life?
Where did I see Jesus as better this week than the thing I was leaning on?
What question did this passage raise that I want to bring to my pastor or Micah?
